analysis.title: The Selling Is Spreading
key_insights: Tech selloff is broadening: semis (SOX) are down 12% from the October 6 high, Korea's memory-chip weakness is spreading across the tech complex, and China's hard-tech stocks keep falling despite oversold readings.
The Market Ear's common theme is crowded trades, deteriorating momentum and a growing risk of a broader positioning unwind.
DXY keeps rising after breaking above its main range and pausing near 102. The next major resistance is a long-term downward-sloping trend line near 105. RSI is elevated but not extreme.

ING says net USD longs versus G10 currencies excluding JPY are 24% of open interest and options risk reversals are near prior extremes. ING sees no obvious catalyst for a reversal because Fed expectations are supportive and global bond weakness supports the dollar.

Deutsche Bank turned tactically cautious on tech just before the selloff, arguing the latest rotation into the sector is near exhaustion. Mega-cap growth and tech have about 4 points of relative upside to the top of the long-term trend channel versus potentially 16 points of downside if past rotation patterns repeat.
This is the fifth major rotation into tech in two years, and previous reversals tended to be sharp, inverted V-shaped moves.

NDX is back in the middle of its long-running range, where the trend line since April and the 100-day moving average converge. The Market Ear sees little edge in trading the middle of a range but says the aggressive price action should not be dismissed.
SOX is well below its 100-day moving average but above the 200-day. RSI is at its most oversold since late July, and 11,200 is the level to watch.
KOSPI is described as one of the main pillars of the global AI trade, and weakness there is no longer isolated to Korean memory.
The price analog to the 1998-2000 internet bubble suggests the rally is nearing its climax, though valuation differences could make the analog break down sooner.
China's STAR 50 is below its 50- and 200-day moving averages with RSI at its most oversold on record. The index is concentrated in hard tech, particularly semiconductors.
Goldman Sachs notes Chinese semiconductor stocks trade at a 237% forward P/E premium to global peers and warns that overpaying for growth and policy support is a key risk.

Europe faces pressure from French rates and surging TTF gas prices. France's fiscal problems are being built into the euro's risk premium, and markets already price a December ECB hike, leaving limited room for hawkish surprises.
Silver broke below the trend line in place since April 2025 and is testing $56. A close below it leaves little support until about $48.
